newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NRB shares jump on robust prospect views.
newsitem.headline: NRB shares jump on robust prospect views.

text.p: Shares in banking firm New Republic Bank (NRB) soared over 20 percent towards the close of trade on Thursday on perceptions the firm was in line for strong earnings growth and would secure a hefty workload, dealers said.

The shares soared and closed at a new year high of 700 cents after broker Cahn Shapiro bought 2,000 shares first at 650 cents and then another 3,000 at 700 cents. The share closed on Wednesday at 580 cents.
The day's overall volumes were heavy at over 2.6 million shares, the bulk of which traded in a bookover deal by Mathison & Hollidge, which is part of the NRB group.
Colin Goldstein, portfolio manager at brokerage Cahn Shapiro said that a line of shares, which had been holding the market down, had been taken out leaving the share free to move up.

"(NRB chairman and owner) Dato Samsudin has got rid of most of the debt load. We expect a lot of corporate work to flow from Malaysia and the interim and final earnings are going to be very good," Goldstein told Reuters.
Samsudin, a Malaysian businessman who has settled in South Africa, has been actively buying up investments in the country's property and banking industry.
"The interim and final earnings are going to be very good," Goldstein said.

In the year ended March 31, 1997 NRB reported earnings per share of 20.7 cents compared with 20.6 cents a year ago, a vast improvement on the fall to 8.2 cents at the 1996 half year stage from 24.1 cents before.
NRB pyramid holding firm SMG Holdings Ltd in February announced it had bought Mathison & Hollidge.
